text:
Ben Kindel made Pittsburgh's opening roster at 19, a year after the Penguins took him 11th overall out of the WHL's Calgary Hitmen, and he has 7 points in 15 games on more than 17 minutes a night. He missed a stretch in late October, came back, and has been practicing with the first power-play unit.

His point total undersells how he has played. The Penguins have scored 9.8 fewer goals than their chances deserve with him on the ice, the kind of cold run that tends to swing back. His own shooting is a bit low too, 9.4% against a range closer to 12%.

The context helps. Forwards drafted 6th to 16th since 2005 scored a median 0.37 points a game in their first full season; he is at 0.47. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking has him carrying the puck in on 56% of his entries, which is a veteran's habit. Our projection is about 41 points. For a teenager in a top-nine role, that would be a very good year.
headline: Kindel's rookie numbers are better than his luck
